findings.evidence: Line 237-239 statement is purely `∀ᵐ`; `abs_eq_of_normalizedExpProfile_eq` at line 220 is `private`.
findings.fix: Reword both to the a.e. statement, or make the set bound a public statement (e.g. `{t | f t = g t} ⊆ {x, -x}`) and cite that.
findings.issue: Docstring claims the two normalised exponentials "agree at no more than two points", but the statement only gives `∀ᵐ t ∂volume.restrict (Icc tLo tHi), … ≠ …`; the two-point bound is proof-internal (private `abs_eq_of_normalizedExpProfile_eq`, line 220). Same overclaim in the module docstring, line 22-23, which cites this theorem for it.

findings.evidence: `tIntegrate_normalizedExpProfile` (line 205) requires `h : tLo < tHi`; `tIntegrate_expProfile_pos` (line 166) likewise, so positivity of the divisor is unavailable on a degenerate range.
findings.fix: Qualify the docstring: normalised to integrate to one when `tLo < tHi`, pointing at `tIntegrate_normalizedExpProfile`.
findings.issue: `normalizedExpProfile` is documented as "normalised to integrate to one over `[tLo, tHi]`", which is false for `tLo = tHi`: the divisor `tIntegrate tLo tHi (expProfile B)` is 0 there, so the function is identically 0 and integrates to 0.

findings.evidence: Lines 205-209 carry no `/-- … -/`; contrast lines 211-212 and 235-236.
findings.fix: Add a one-line docstring stating that the normalised exponential integrates to one over a range of positive length.
findings.issue: `tIntegrate_normalizedExpProfile`, a main result of the non-uniqueness section (the normalisation-to-one statement the rest of the section rests on), has no docstring, while the surrounding results do.

summary: The module docstring is mathematical, accurate in structure, and free of roadmap/process narrative, but two docstrings promise more than the statements deliver (an 'at most two points' bound that only the private lemma proves, and normalisation-to-one that fails on degenerate ranges), and one headline theorem is undocumented.
